gap: No result ChatGPT got gives today's maker-store prices for the units it named: the only EcoFlow pick with a documented USB UPS data link that we could price on us.ecoflow.com today is the DELTA 3 Ultra series at $1,299 (Ultra Plus $1,599). The DELTA 3 Classic ($479) and DELTA 3 ($579) on the same store sit 2.2–2.7x cheaper, and the Classic's listing says its 10 ms auto-switch keeps 'NAS systems and servers' running, but no source we opened documents a data port on either.
standout_why: Compared against computingforgeeks.com/power-station-vs-ups-homelab (top result), thepowerstationguide.com/blog/portable-power-station-vs-ups (cited) and racksandwatts.com. ComputingForGeeks already gives rough 'about' prices (RIVER 3 Plus about $299, C1000 Gen 2 about $570, AC180 about $449, Jackery 1000 v2 about $499, CP1500PFCLCD about $240), with no date and no store. The Power Station Guide and Racks and Watts give no prices at all. Today's maker-store prices are new: AC180 is $499 today, not about $449, and the DELTA 3 Ultra series is $1,299. But we could not price the two picks that decide the answer (RIVER 3 Plus and DELTA 3 Plus standalone), so this is only a partial improvement.
decides: This supports the current structure: the USB-signalling picks are EcoFlow-only, and the cheapest one we priced today (DELTA 3 Ultra, $1,299) costs far more than the no-data-port stations at $479–$619. The page should warn that EcoFlow's $479 DELTA 3 Classic listing names NAS systems in its 10 ms auto-switch line without a documented shutdown link. The RIVER 3 Plus stays the budget pick, but its price has to be re-read before publishing because the store wouldn't serve it today.
